reference.source: Sleisenger and Fordtran's Gastrointestinal and Liver Disease
clinicalPearls: A benign, non-inflammatory hyperplastic change of the gallbladder wall characterised by mucosal overgrowth and outpouchings into a thickened muscular layer
The pathognomonic feature is Rokitansky-Aschoff sinuses, mucosal invaginations that extend into the wall
Often asymptomatic and found incidentally, though some patients have biliary-type pain, particularly with the segmental (fundal) form
On ultrasound, small cystic intramural spaces and the characteristic comet-tail (ring-down) reverberation artefact from cholesterol crystals within the sinuses are highly suggestive
Described as diffuse, segmental, or localised (fundal), with the segmental form sometimes producing an hourglass configuration
MRI shows the intramural sinuses as a string-of-beads or pearl-necklace appearance on heavily T2-weighted sequences
It is a benign condition, so asymptomatic disease needs no treatment; cholecystectomy is reserved for symptoms or when imaging cannot confidently exclude malignancy
reference.pathophysiology: Adenomyomatosis is a hyperplastic, degenerative change rather than an inflammatory or neoplastic one. Proliferation of the surface epithelium together with hypertrophy of the muscularis leads to thickening of the gallbladder wall, and the mucosa herniates through the muscular layer to form Rokitansky-Aschoff sinuses, epithelium-lined intramural diverticula. Bile stagnating within these sinuses tends to deposit cholesterol crystals and small calculi, which generate the characteristic comet-tail reverberation artefact on ultrasound. The process may be diffuse, may affect a segment (often producing focal narrowing), or may be localised to the fundus as a mass-like nodule. Although benign, focal and segmental forms can mimic gallbladder carcinoma and can occasionally coexist with it, which is the principal diagnostic concern.
additionalDifferentials: Wall thickening from adjacent hepatic or systemic disease
additionalInvestigations: High-resolution ultrasound to detect intramural cystic spaces and comet-tail artefacts
MRI with heavily T2-weighted sequences to show the pearl-necklace sign of Rokitansky-Aschoff sinuses
Contrast-enhanced imaging when focal thickening cannot be distinguished from carcinoma
Endoscopic ultrasound for detailed assessment of the wall layers in equivocal cases
Liver function tests and CA 19-9 if malignancy is a concern
Histological examination of the resected specimen for definitive diagnosis
redFlags: Focal or segmental wall thickening that cannot be confidently distinguished from carcinoma
An enhancing soft-tissue mass or irregular wall on cross-sectional imaging
New or progressive symptoms with concerning imaging features
reference.prognosis: The condition is benign with an excellent prognosis; asymptomatic disease requires no intervention, and cholecystectomy is curative when performed for symptoms or diagnostic uncertainty.
pitfalls: Mistaking focal or segmental adenomyomatosis for gallbladder carcinoma, or the reverse
Overlooking a coexisting malignancy within an area of wall thickening
Recommending surgery for confidently benign, asymptomatic disease
Failing to recognise the specific comet-tail and pearl-necklace imaging signs
Attributing all right upper quadrant symptoms to adenomyomatosis without excluding other causes
references: Sleisenger and Fordtran's Gastrointestinal and Liver Disease
Radiology reviews of gallbladder adenomyomatosis imaging
management: Reassure and adopt conservative observation for asymptomatic disease found incidentally, as the condition is benign
Offer laparoscopic cholecystectomy for biliary-type symptoms, which is curative
Proceed to cholecystectomy when focal or segmental wall thickening cannot be reliably distinguished from gallbladder carcinoma
Characterise lesions with high-resolution ultrasound, heavily T2-weighted MRI and, where needed, contrast-enhanced imaging or endoscopic ultrasound to demonstrate Rokitansky-Aschoff sinuses
Confirm the diagnosis histologically on the resected specimen
Undertake interval imaging surveillance in equivocal cases where malignancy remains a concern
